column3: Description

The signal "Existence probability - detection level" of the detection uses, for example, signal to noise ratio(SNR) and radar cross section(RCS). It is not based on history.

Additional information:
Use as confidence measure where a low value means less confidence and a high value indicates strong confidence.

The signal "Detection ID" provides the unique identification number of the detection within the detection list.

Additional information:
The signal's "Detection ID" value is only unique for each sensor cluster's detection entities of DLI within one measurement cycle
If interfaces use the signal "Detection ID" to link, for example, object entities with detection entities, the interfaces shall ensure the unambiguity of the referenced entities at each or multiple measurement cycle [see, for example, cross interface optimisation "Source entities of a derived signal".

The signal's "Object ID" value defines the object to which this detection is associated to; invlid = "no associated object", for example, for the first detection cycle of the entity.

Additional information:
Refers to object (for example, potentially moving object) with the highest probability.
The signal's "Object ID reference - detection level" value could reference entities of the sensor cluster's OLI or entities which are used internally by the sensor cluster.
Alternative A2I: The mapping of object signal "Object ID" and detections signal "Object ID reference - detection level" could be provided in a separate interface.

The signal "Radar cross section" provides the RCS of the detection.

Additional information:
It is the representative RCS of the detection.
The value is compensated. Slow changes (for example, aging of the sensor) are compensated, fast changes (for example, rain) are not compensated. All systematic absorptions are compensated, for example, from the bumper.
The signal "Radar cross section - error" provides the error value of the signal "Radar cross section".

column3: The signal "Multi target probability" describes the possibility if more than one real-world object has led to this detection.

Ambiguous measurement uses one ID for signal "Ambiguity grouping ID" for ambiguous detection candidates. Ambiguous detections (all detection candidates for the same measurement value) are shown by the same signal's "Ambiguity grouping ID" value.
Detections of unambiguous measurements have signal "Ambiguity grouping ID" := 0.

Additional information:
Ambiguity can be specified by, for example, the signal "Radial velocity ambiguity domain {begin, end}", "Range ambiguity domain {begin, end}", "Angle azimuth ambiguity domain {begin, end}" or "Angle elevation ambiguity domain {begin, end}". Other ambiguities can add an additional signal analogous to these signals.
The signal's "Ambiguity grouping ID" value in the list is unique only for each cycle. The signal's "Ambiguity grouping ID" values could be reused every cycle.

column3:
The signal "Detection ambiguity probability" provides the probability for different hypotheses, sum is less or equal 100% for all detections with the same signal's "Ambiguity grouping ID" value.

Additional information:
Use as confidence measure where a low value means less confidence and a high value indicates strong confidence.

The signal "Free space probability" provides the free space probability in the range [0, 100] % from the origin of the sensor up to this detection, as given by the distance.

Additional information:
The probability of free space between the origin and this detection as given by the distance in the range [0, 100] %. In this range, for example, the signal "Signal to noise ratio - detection level" is very low. A second detection (detection behind another detection) has the signal "Free space probability" = 0%.
In case of an empty measurement, the detection's signal "Existence probability - detection level" is set to 0% and the distance is set to default value. The distance of the detection combined with the signal "Free space probability" give the free space.
Use as confidence measure where a low value means less confidence and a high value indicates strong confidence.

The signal "Number of valid detection classifications" provides the current number of valid tuples for detection classifications. The tuples are defined by the signals "Detection classification type" and "Detection classification type - confidence"
